violation_type.title: Director Responsibilities - Employee Assignments (26 TAC §746.1003(3))
violation_type.typical_finding: The director assigned a caregiver assignments that did not match their skills, abilities, and training.

finding_variants.text: The director assigned a caregiver assignments that did not match their skills, abilities, and training.

Through an investigation, it was determined that director's responsibilities were not being met when a staff member was placed in a classroom where they could not perform all job duties and meet the children's care requirements.
A caregiver did not have the skills or abilities needed to care for children in the 2?3-year-old classroom. This resulted in using excessive force during nap time.

This was evaluated as part of a DFPS investigation and found deficient.   Based on information provided a caregiver was assigned to a classroom where multiple employees stated the caregiver had difficulty managing.
Based on information gathered, the director did not ensure the caregiver's job assignment matched their abilities.
The director failed to follow up with staff after a parent express their concerns their child was not being taken the restroom for potty training and pull-ups were not being changed.

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Employee Assignments: Through DFPS interviews it was established that the caregiver in question experienced difficulties with classroom management while working alone in the classroom. Despite these known issues the caregiver, continued to work alone in the same classroom.

Director Responsibilities - Employee Assignments: The director failed to provide appropriate guidance or intervene when a caregiver yelled at, pursued, and dragged a child into the classroom while refusing to allow the child to enter. The director reported inaccurate details concerning a child's injury without conducting appropriate observation or clarification of the incident.

Director Responsibilities - Employee Assignments: A caregiver was observed providing director care for infants in the Oaks I and Oaks II classroom without completing on boarding. The operation does not have any completed paperwork for the caregiver. The operations has not completed orientation with caregiver. The operation has not verified the caregiver has qualifying previous experience. When asked, the caregiver was not knowledge of basic infant needs or standard requirements.
Director Responsibilities - Employee Assignments: During an unannounced inspection, a caregiver was observed to be frustrated with a child who  has special needs.

Director Responsibilities - Employee Assignments: The director assigned a person to be a driver/caregiver and was aware that the person was not supposed to be alone with a child or group of children in care, including transportation. The person was also allowed to transport children without a valid driver?s license.
Director Responsibilities - Employee Assignments: Based on information gathered, the director did not ensure the caregiver's job assignment matched their abilities.

Based on the needs and abilities of the children, an additional caregiver should have been placed in the classroom for proper oversight.

Director Responsibilities - Employee Assignments: Based on the information gathered during the DFPS investigation, it was concluded the director allowed one caregiver to be responsible for 8 children which included 3 children with special needs, and 1 infant. A child managed to exit the operation without caregiver's knowledge.

Director Responsibilities - Employee Assignments: It is found though investigation evidence a staff was assigned a classroom when they did not have the skills to safely supervise the entire group in care.

The evidence shows that the director failed to provide adequate support to a caregiver who was struggling with a child's behavior. Director Responsibilities - Employee Assignments: This standard was tasked as part of an investigation and found deficient. Director Responsibilities - Employee Assignments: During the DFPS investigation, an infant room caregiver stated that she was not allowed to carry any children due to her high-risk pregnancy. The caregiver was left alone in the room to care for the infants while the other caregiver was called to the front door to attend to parents picking up their children. The caregiver was unable to properly care for the injured infant and infants in care due to her health restriction.
